objective: Test the smallest causal ABI construct: whether an already-qualified frozen-teacher grammar signal can be converted into segregated search-only training material and produce a prompt-specific held-out behavioral improvement in the exact Phase 2 LayerCake host.

source_artifact.qualification: 224/224 positive counterbalanced forced-choice grammar preferences; validation is 64/64 and remains excluded from training

runs: same rows, seed, optimizer budget, and host with a SHA-256-seeded target derangement

primary_per_row_measures: mean log probability of the exact correct completion

all_required: real candidate improves held-out correct-completion mean log probability over the unchanged parent with paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound greater than zero
real candidate improves held-out correct-completion mean log probability over the shuffled-target control with paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound greater than zero
real candidate improves held-out correct-minus-incorrect margin over the unchanged parent with paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound greater than zero
real candidate improves held-out correct-minus-incorrect margin over the shuffled-target control with paired-bootstrap 95% lower bound greater than zero
real candidate positive-margin accuracy is at least 0.75
all 64 validation rows are evaluated and none were used for training
only route 0 changes; the shared core, classifier, and other nine task cakes remain byte-identical in logical tensor state
source artifact remains byte-identical and no source teacher, source block, source weight, or source tokenizer is present in the deployed candidate

decision_rule: Run exactly the preregistered real and shuffled acquisitions once. PASS proves only a bounded teacher-artifact-to-LayerCake grammar transfer construct. FAIL is preserved as negative evidence and ends this pass without nearby sweeps.
claim_boundary: A passing pilot does not prove fluent English extraction, automatic labeling, knowledge segregation beyond the manually scoped grammar catalog, minimality, domain transfer, or teacher-level generational parity.
